recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write both as fractions
steps.margin_note: tan and cot are both ratios of sine and cosine. Writing them out is what lets them be added over a common denominator.

recall.must_convey: That tanA and cotA are written as sinA/cosA and cosA/sinA.
accept: write tan A as sin A over cos A and cot A as cos A over sin A
express both in terms of sine and cosine
convert tan and cot into fractions
tan A ni sin A by cos A ga, cot A ni cos A by sin A ga rasta
put both over sine and cosine

steps.why: Almost every identity of this kind starts by reducing everything to sine and cosine — from there the algebra is ordinary fractions.
common_mistakes: Leaving tan and cot as they are and looking for a formula.
steps.memory_tip: tan and cot are both ratios of sine and cosine — write them out to add over a common denominator.

steps.label: Add over a common denominator
steps.margin_note: The numerator becomes sin²A + cos²A, which is 1 — the identity that makes this whole question short.

recall.must_convey: That the two fractions are added, the numerator becomes sin²A + cos²A, and that equals 1.
accept: add them over a common denominator, the numerator is sin squared plus cos squared which is one
combine the fractions and use the Pythagorean identity
the top becomes one leaving one over sin A cos A
common denominator lo add cheste numerator one avthundi
sin square plus cos square is one

steps.why: sin²A + cos²A = 1 is the single most used identity in the chapter, and this is the cleanest place it appears.
common_mistakes: Adding the numerators without a common denominator.
steps.memory_tip: The numerator is sin²A + cos²A, which is 1 — the identity that makes this short.

steps.label: Introduce the double angle
steps.margin_note: First mark. The answer is in 2A, so a 2A has to be manufactured. Multiplying top and bottom by 2 turns 2 sinA cosA into sin2A.

recall.must_convey: That top and bottom are multiplied by 2 so the denominator becomes sin 2A.
accept: multiply top and bottom by two so two sin A cos A becomes sin two A
make a two on the bottom to get sin two A
introduce the double angle by doubling numerator and denominator
rendu vaipula two tho multiply cheste sin two A vasthundi
two sin A cos A is sin two A

steps.why: The right-hand side is in 2A and the left in A, so the proof has to cross between them. The 2 is introduced deliberately, not found.
common_mistakes: Writing sinA cosA = sin2A without the 2.
steps.memory_tip: The answer is in 2A, so manufacture one: doubling top and bottom turns 2 sinA cosA into sin2A.

steps.label: Convert to cosec
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 1/sin is cosec, so 2/sin2A is 2 cosec2A. Name the reciprocal rather than leaving the fraction.

accept: two over sin two A is two cosec two A
one over sine is cosec so the answer is two cosec two A
convert the fraction to cosec
one by sin ante cosec, so two cosec two A
the answer is two cosec two A

steps.why: The question asks for the cosec form, so the last line must read 2 cosec 2A — stopping at 2/sin 2A leaves the proof unfinished.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 2/sin2A, which leaves the proof unfinished.
steps.memory_tip: 1/sin is cosec, so 2/sin2A is 2 cosec 2A. Name the reciprocal.

insider_note: Adding over sinA cosA makes the numerator sin²A + cos²A = 1 at once. Doubling top and bottom then turns the denominator into sin2A.
